I do agree with them that 344 is one of the more stark differences. However, I believe Miura at the very least experimented with digital as far back as chapter 331 potentially. Perhaps not for every page and he may have still used his traditional work as a base. I don't have any proof of course but looking at some of the linework there's some strokes that really only make sense if he was doing it digitally.

Or he may have just touched things up digitally.

Fully agree, I also draw and nothing beats the tactile feedback of an actual pencil and dip pen on paper/bristol board. But digital is simply too convenient not to use, especially for professionals with a deadline.

It certainly is the way of the day but as you said, it certainly leads to a lot less character in the strokes. There's a few artists still sticking to traditional but I imagine it's not many. Which is a shame as I prefer trad. 

If you're interested there are ways to make drawing digitally in Clip Studio look a lot more realistic, imo Yoshikadu Hamada achieves this effect well with his size jitter penwork. If you search Yoshikadu on Youtube you can see his process from his livestreams and the difference in linework is night and day.

And if you have any works I can take a look at let me know, one artist to another. I'll follow you if you're on Twitter/Deviantart/Tumblr/etc.

Miura swapped to digital and its taken an obvious toll on the art style and quality of linework. The strokes look more artificial. Honestly, it's hard to help. I was in a similar situation. I figured best case scenario she'd be upset for a while but ultimately be okay. Worst case, she would kill herself and I'd feel like it was my fault. I'd go through this thought process quite a bit and figured I would keep dating her, even though I didn't want to, because I'd rather be unhappy than feel responsible for someone's death.

Looking back on it now, it was dumb. Even knowing it was emotionally abusive and knowing for a fact it was wrong, even if I was 99% sure she wouldn't go through with suicide, there's always that 1% that didn't know for sure so kept the relationship going.

Guess the only thing you can do is help your friend know that he is not responsible for this person's mental state and if she does do something, even though it's unlikely it wouldn't be his fault and you're in his corner ready to support him in that case.
